claims.claim: Reverb runs on an event loop, as a Go server would; both hold a connection as a small amount of memory, not a thread
claims.why: Reverb was not benchmarked, and per-connection memory for WebSocket servers was not measured.

claims.claim: Go does use less memory per connection than Reverb
claims.why: The PHP entries are Laravel over FPM or Octane, not Reverb, and no long-lived WebSocket connections were measured.

claims.claim: A simple Go server with read and write buffers per connection often uses tens of KB per connection
claims.measured: go-nethttp: 15 MB peak at 256 connections vs 2 MB idle, roughly 50 KB per connection; go-gin: 16 MB vs 2 MB, roughly 55 KB per connection
claims.why: Peak minus idle memory, divided by connections, gives roughly 50 KB per HTTP keep-alive connection, which is tens of KB, though these are HTTP connections, not WebSocket ones.

claims.claim: If Reverb uses even 50 KB per connection, 150,000–200,000 connections need about 10 GB of RAM
claims.why: Reverb's per-connection memory was not measured, so the 50 KB input can't be checked.

claims.claim: The default stream_select loop cannot go past about 1,024 connections per process
claims.why: The benchmark did not test Reverb or its event-loop backends.

claims.claim: Each Reverb process uses a single core
claims.why: Each server ran with only 1 CPU and Reverb was not included, so multi-core use can't be judged.

claims.claim: Centrifugo is built to handle very large numbers of connections
Soketi is fast and light on memory
claims.why: Soketi was not benchmarked, and the Node servers that were measured (Express, Fastify) are different software.
